introduction_markdown:

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the equipment that is used to:

(i) Transfer 25 cm$^3$ of the $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ into a conical flask.

(ii) Name the equipment in which the acid is filled. *[2 marks]*

(iii) How is the conical flask usually cleaned before use in titration? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **pipette** (25 cm$^3$ pipette, used with a pipette filler).

(ii) A **burette**.

(iii) It is **rinsed with distilled water** only. It may be left wet, because water does not change the amount of sodium carbonate in the flask; it must **not** be rinsed with the carbonate solution or the acid, which would change the amount of reactant.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the table and calculate the mean.

(i) Complete the table. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Calculate the average titre used. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Titre = final reading - initial reading (in cm$^3$):

| Titration | Approximate | 1st Accurate | 2nd Accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial | 0.0 | 22.7 | 0.0 |
| Final | 22.7 | 45.3 | 22.6 |
| Titre | **22.7** | **22.6** | **22.6** |

(ii) The approximate titre is only a rough guide and is not used. The two accurate titres agree (22.6 and 22.6 cm$^3$):

Average titre = $\dfrac{22.6 + 22.6}{2} =$ **22.6 cm$^3$**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give a suitable indicator used in the titration and state the colour change observed.

Indicator: ................

Colour change: initial colour ................ final colour ................ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Indicator: methyl orange** (a strong acid is added to a weakly basic carbonate solution, so an indicator that changes in the acid range is suitable).

- Initial colour (in the sodium carbonate in the flask): **yellow**.
- Final colour (at the end point, when the acid is just in excess): **orange** (turning pink-red with more acid).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Determine the concentration of the $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ solution in mol/dm$^3$.

$\mathrm{Na_2CO_3} + 2\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaNO_3} + \mathrm{CO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Volume of acid (average titre) = 22.6 cm$^3$ = 0.0226 dm$^3$.

Amount of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ = $0.02 \times 0.0226 = 4.52 \times 10^{-4}$ mol

From the equation, 2 mol $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ react with 1 mol $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$:

Amount of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ = $\dfrac{4.52 \times 10^{-4}}{2} = 2.26 \times 10^{-4}$ mol (in the 25 cm$^3$ pipetted)

Concentration = $\dfrac{2.26 \times 10^{-4}}{0.025} =$ **$9.04 \times 10^{-3}$ mol/dm$^3$** (0.00904 mol/dm$^3$)

questions.enonce_markdown:
In order to prepare a dry sample of carbon dioxide, you were provided with the following: dilute nitric acid, solid sodium carbonate, concentrated sulphuric acid, thistle funnel, 2 flat bottom flasks, delivery tube, rubber bungs, gas collecting jar.

**EITHER** Draw the experimental set up that was used to prepare a pure dry sample of carbon dioxide gas.

**OR** Describe how the equipment and chemicals are arranged and used to prepare a pure dry sample of carbon dioxide gas. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Reaction: $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3(s)} + 2\mathrm{HNO_3(aq)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaNO_3(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)} + \mathrm{CO_2(g)}$

*Arrangement (what to draw, or to describe, in order from left to right):*

1. **Flask 1** (generator): a flat-bottomed flask containing **solid sodium carbonate**, closed by a rubber bung through which pass a **thistle funnel** (its lower end dipping **below the level of the acid**, which is poured in as **dilute nitric acid**) and a delivery tube.
2. **Flask 2** (drying flask): a flat-bottomed flask containing **concentrated sulphuric acid**, which dries the gas. The delivery tube from flask 1 dips **below the surface of the acid**; a second, short delivery tube leaves from above the acid.
3. A **gas jar** to collect the gas by **upward delivery (downward displacement of air)**: the delivery tube reaches the bottom of the jar because carbon dioxide is **denser than air**. (It is not collected over water, because the gas would not be dry.)

Label: thistle funnel, dilute nitric acid, sodium carbonate, conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (drying agent), gas jar, carbon dioxide.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following set up is used by a student to separate a solid mixture of $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ and NaCl.

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(i) Name the apparatus B.

(ii) Why was the solid mixture heated? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **B is the evaporating dish** (china dish) holding the solid mixture.

(ii) On heating, **ammonium chloride sublimes**: it changes directly from solid to vapour, while **sodium chloride does not**. The vapour rises, **condenses as a white solid on the cooler walls of the inverted funnel**, and the sodium chloride is left in the dish. The two solids are thus separated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why are the following usually used in the laboratory?

(i) Handgloves.

(ii) Safety googles. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Handgloves** protect the hands from corrosive, toxic or irritating chemicals and from hot apparatus.

(ii) **Safety goggles** protect the eyes from splashes of chemicals, harmful fumes and flying particles.
